The 6 h last-good rule of the spec matches LASTGOOD_TTL_SECONDS = 6 * 3600 at quota.ts:91 and the >= compare at quota.ts:369.

The plan point 8 text matches the drivers: it names the exact export values and 'timeout 90 ra-quota status --json' (plan.md, row 4.13r point 8); the drivers run 'timeout 90 "$BENCH_RA_QUOTA" status --json' with BENCH_RA_QUOTA at the named path (probe-4.10.sh:16,55; night-4.11.sh:16,70). The last-good file /tmp/ra-quota-lastgood.json holds plans.opencode-go with fetchedAt age 0.01 h and the same 5h and weekly values, so the fallback stands fresh.

The probe answer: the 01:45 probe can give each of the 3 pilot routes a real result. The wiring no longer blocks it: both Go routes read the quota through ra-quota at the driver level (90 s bound) and the runner level (90 s bound, last-good fallback), and the live values sit at 7.41 and 17.57 percent. The remaining conditions: (1) the shared credential store holds exactly one active entry with integrationID opencode-go for routes 1 and 3, and one with opencode for route 2; a missing or ambiguous entry refuses the seed exactly as at 04:35; (2) the ra-quota read succeeds within 90 s at probe time, or the last-good file holds a usable reading younger than 6 h; (3) the Go windows stay under 5h 95 and weekly 100 at probe time; (4) each real call returns a non-empty answer within 600 s, on one of its 3 attempts, else the route records unreachable; (5) all three routes start before the 05:55 window end; (6) for the pilot passes, night 1 at 02:00 greps the probe file 15 minutes after the probe start, so routes that complete after 02:00 are skipped in night 1 (see N4); nights 2 and 3 read the completed file.
